title: Propagation, Transplant Identity and Sanitation Control

content.overview: Propagation work multiplies both desired genetics and preventable errors. Technician I learners practice confirming donor, lot, tray and work-order identity before cutting or transplanting; preparing a clean work area; following the supplied cutting, rooting or transplant sequence; protecting labels and counts through movement; observing rooting or seedling condition; and documenting losses or exceptions without guessing identity or changing the propagation method outside authorization.

vocabulary.definition: The controlled plant or lot identity from which vegetative propagation material is taken.
A root that develops from tissue other than an existing root, such as the stem of a vegetative cutting.
A controlled transition from protected propagation conditions toward the normal production environment.
A loss or uncertainty in the documented relationship between plant material and its required donor, lot, tray or plant identity.

sections.title: Seed germination is a staged physiological transition
sections.body: A dry viable seed first takes up water by imbibition. Hydration restores membrane function, activates enzymes and respiration, and allows the embryo to resume growth. The radicle normally emerges first and establishes the initial root axis; the hypocotyl and cotyledons then support emergence and early seedling development. Water is essential, but persistent saturation can reduce oxygen diffusion and favor failure. Temperature changes reaction rates, while seed age and storage history influence viability and vigor.

sections.title: Identity is verified before plant material moves
sections.body: Before taking cuttings, sowing assigned seed, transplanting or moving trays, verify the controlled donor or source, lot or batch, tray and destination required by the work order. If labels are missing or conflicting, stop movement and resolve identity from approved records; leaf shape or memory is not a valid substitute.

sections.title: Fresh tissue increases sanitation consequence
sections.body: Cut surfaces and young propagation material are vulnerable to contamination and water stress. Use the supplied tool, glove, surface and movement sanitation steps, and do not carry a blade or other contact tool from suspect material into clean material without the required control step.

sections.title: Follow the method; record biological variation
sections.body: Genotype, donor condition, cutting quality and environment can change rooting behavior. Technician I follows the assigned method and records rooting, loss or acclimatization differences by identified batch rather than changing humidity, rooting treatment or handling strategy independently because one cultivar is slower.

sections.title: Counts and labels stay attached to reality
sections.body: Propagation records should preserve starting quantity, losses, usable plants and movement or transplant status with the correct identity. Missing or uncertain material is documented as an exception instead of being relabeled to make the count reconcile.

workedExamples: Two freshly cut trays are found without labels. The technician stops movement and uses the approved discrepancy process rather than guessing cultivar identity from appearance.

One identified cultivar roots more slowly than the rest under the same supplied procedure. The technician records the genotype-specific trend and escalates if it exceeds the defined expectation instead of changing the entire propagation environment without authorization.
commonMistakes: Taking material before donor identity is confirmed.
Reusing contact tools across suspect and clean material without the required sanitation step.
Guessing the identity of an unlabeled tray.
Changing propagation conditions independently because one batch roots more slowly.
content.practicalApplication: Complete a simulated propagation work order that includes one donor-label mismatch, a sanitation checkpoint, a tray-count discrepancy and a slower-rooting identified batch. Use the downloadable propagation workstation practice sheet to preserve identity, count reconciliation, sanitation/quarantine status, authorized decisions and handoff evidence.
content.summary: Propagation quality depends on identity control, sanitation, controlled execution and truthful records. Technician I protects the donor-to-tray chain, follows the supplied method, records biological variation and escalates exceptions rather than guessing or improvising.

items.title: Verify the work order
items.body: Confirm donor/source, lot or batch, requested quantity, tray or destination and current instructions.

items.title: Prepare the clean workstation
items.body: Complete the required surface, tool, glove and material sanitation steps before handling propagation material.

items.title: Protect identity during handling
items.body: Keep labels and counts associated with the correct donor, tray or plant through cutting, rooting, transplant and movement.

items.title: Follow the authorized method
items.body: Use the supplied preparation, rooting or transplant sequence without independent process redesign.

items.title: Observe and count
items.body: Record rooting/seedling condition, losses, usable material and meaningful exceptions by identity.

items.title: Escalate discrepancies
items.body: Stop and route label, count, contamination or abnormal-condition problems that cannot be resolved within procedure.

blocks.title: Seed anatomy and germination physiology
blocks.alt: Educational cannabis seed cutaway and germination sequence identifying seed coat, embryo, cotyledons and radicle, followed by water uptake, radicle emergence and early seedling establishment.
blocks.caption: Germination moves from water uptake and metabolic reactivation to radicle emergence and seedling establishment. Moisture, oxygen, temperature, sanitation and seed vigor interact throughout the process.

blocks.title: Propagation identity and traceability workflow
blocks.alt: Workflow from verified donor and work-order identity through staged labels, authorized propagation, count reconciliation and a stop-and-hold response for identity conflicts.
blocks.caption: Identity is verified before plant material moves. Uncertain identity is held and resolved from approved evidence rather than guessed.

blocks.title: Biosecurity and quarantine workflow
blocks.alt: Clean-to-dirty movement diagram showing sanitation checkpoints, suspect material isolation, quarantine boundaries, breach documentation and escalation.
blocks.caption: Propagation sanitation includes movement control. Suspect material, tools or breaches are contained and documented before clean work resumes.

blocks.title: Unlabeled propagation trays
blocks.setting: Two trays of fresh cuttings become separated from their labels before movement to the propagation area.
blocks.prompt: What is the strongest Technician I response?
options: Stop movement and resolve identity through the approved record/discrepancy process
Combine the trays because they were cut on the same shift
Relabel both as the most common cultivar
blocks.answer: Stop movement and resolve identity through the approved record/discrepancy process
blocks.feedback: Propagation traceability depends on preserving donor and batch identity. An uncertain identity remains a discrepancy until it is resolved through approved evidence.
